claims.text: Cover each type in the fuzz test so test coverage is not weakened.
claims.quote: Would you mind covering each type here already? It doesn't seem to be that complex and otherwise the test is weaker than it needs to be.

claims.text: Avoid dropping the call to DecompressScript with different nSize.
claims.quote: I guess this coverage wasn't that interesting but this is dropping the call of `DecompressScript` with different `nSize`.
claims.status_note: reviewer dropped the point noting the coverage was not that important, and author further clarified coverage of raw scripts
claims.status_by_quote: as I said, not that important coverage I guess

claims.text: Run the check once instead of 1,000 times in the unit test, or move it to fuzz testing.
claims.quote: Do we really need to check this 1000 times? If we do, then maybe this should rather be a fuzz test? For a unit test doing this once should suffice I think.

claims.text: Extract off-curve and wrong-Y raw-storage assertions into a shared helper function.
claims.quote: Seems to me the off-curve and wrong-Y raw-storage assertions are the same, so could we extract them into a helper?

claims.text: Round-trip compression classes 2 and 3 as well for completeness.
claims.quote: For completeness we could round-trip 2/3 as well

claims.text: Include the compression class and a hex dump of the payload in the decompression failure exception message.
claims.quote: For diagnostics we could include the compression class and a hex dump of the payload as well.

claims.text: Simplify the decodability check in the fuzz test by using XOnlyPubKey.
claims.quote: nit: I think we can simplify this a bit

claims.text: Clarify comment to state that trailing data follows the script in undo records and snapshot files rather than Coin records.
claims.quote:
nit: the script is the last field of a `Coin`, so nothing follows it in a chainstate value.
Undo records and snapshot files are where more data follows.

claims.text: Add unit tests verifying that Coin and CTxUndo deserialization propagate the new script decompression failure.
claims.quote: Given the concern about exceptions being caught along the way (hinted at in the PR description and discussed in several related PRs and issues recently), could we add simple higher-level checks that `Coin` and `CTxUndo` deserialization propagate this new failure?

claims.text: Cap raw-payload consumption in the script fuzz test to leave more fuzzed input for trailing checks.
claims.quote: nit: could we cap raw-payload consumption to leave more fuzz input for later checks?

claims.text: dumptxoutset rollback snapshots skip unreadable coins on decompression failure and can succeed with coins missing.
claims.quote: When `dumptxoutset` creates a rollback snapshot, the copy loop skips coins on read failure. The cursor catches the new decompression exception and returns false, so this PR adds another trigger for that issue. Could we abort the copy on a failed read, either here or in a separate follow-up? Otherwise, `dumptxoutset` can succeed with a coin missing.

claims.text: Return a UTXO read error in scantxoutset when reading a coin fails instead of returning partial results with success: false.
claims.quote: `scantxoutset` uses the same cursor reader, but a failed read currently looks like cancellation (`success: false` with partial results). Could we return the UTXO read error there as well?

claims.text: Perform a round-trip comparison for special scripts in the fuzz test to ensure they re-serialize unchanged.
claims.quote: Indeed, special-scripts were already checked to be decodable and should re-serialize to the same bytes, so a round-trip comparison would check that the script hasn't changed.

support.reason: Looks already pretty solid but I left a few, mostly minor comments.
I see that all decoding errors are reported through exceptions, which is not great. But it means that the error handling in this PR is aligned.
we have lots of similar findings that we should slowly plug, this seems like a good next step
